root_cause.text: UDP wildcard bind conflict detection fails because the decision to use the address-and-port keyed hash (hash2) instead of the port-only hash (hash) was based solely on bucket count (hslot->count > 10), without checking whether the socket being bound has a wildcard source address, causing wildcard binds to incorrectly skip conflict detection against existing specific-address sockets.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `inet_use_hash2_on_bind(sk) &&` before `hslot->count > 10` in `udp_lib_get_port()`, and the new helper returns false when the socket's local address is a wildcard (e.g., `0.0.0.0` or `::`). The CVE description explicitly demonstrates that after binding 11 specific addresses (so hslot->count > 10), a subsequent wildcard bind succeeds unexpectedly because it uses hash2 where the wildcard address does not match the specific addresses stored.
